rubric_assessments.justification: The feedback confirms partial DATE building with DATE(A3+2;A2;A1) formula, though nested incorrectly in OR function.
The feedback explicitly states 'Correctly used DATE(A3+2;A2;A1)' to calculate the anniversary date.
The serial number formula is described as incorrectly nested within OR function, invalidating it as a proper serial number calculation.
The feedback states the student 'Recognized the need for WEEKDAY to identify the day of the week.'
No evidence of computing how many days to add; the formula attempts to add to weekday number incorrectly rather than proper date arithmetic.
The incorrect OR logic with +2 and +1 additions does not represent partial computation of days to add.
The feedback explicitly states 'Missing the required formulas for cells G1, G2, and G3' and CHOOSE was used for text instead of numerical components.
Not all correct - missing G1, G2, G3 formulas and has invalid serial number logic.
Some work was done correctly (DATE function, WEEKDAY), so not 'all wrong / empty'.
DATE function was partially built with =DATE(2025;5;10) in C1, though using hardcoded values instead of cell references.
The feedback confirms 'Correctly used DATE' function in C1: =DATE(2025;5;10).
C1 contains =DATE(2025;5;10) but uses hardcoded values instead of cell references A1, A2, A3, making it not a proper serial number formula in 2 years.
The feedback confirms WEEKDAY function was used, though with hardcoded string instead of cell reference.
E1: =WEEKDAY(E1+2) appears circular and the feedback notes it 'lacks proper formulas' for computing days to add.
The circular reference in E1 does not constitute partial computation of days to add.
G1 contains hardcoded '12', and G2-G3 contain hardcoded values without proper formulas (feedback notes circular references or lacks proper formulas).
Hardcoded values and circular references mean not all correct.
Some work exists (C1 formula, D1, D1, G1 value), so not 'all wrong / empty'.
